title: 06-06-2026 - saturday
body:
i had another one of those school dreams.

at this point, i should probably start paying tuition to my subconscious because i spend more time in dream-school than i ever did in actual college.

for context, i never graduated. financial issues happened, life happened, and unfortunately, universities have this strange requirement called 'money'. 
ever since then, i've had recurring dreams that take place in schools--sometimes with familiar faces, sometimes with strangers my brain manufactures out of thin air.

this dream started innocently enough.

teachers were distributing diplomas.
one by one, students were called forward. some were smiling. some were crying.
everyone seem excited.
to hell i saw my high school classmates i didn't like as well. 

then they called my name.

i walked up and received my diploma.

finally, i thought.

after years of frustration and wondering what could have been, there it was, my diploma. mine. 

for approximately five minutes.

because somehow, somewhere, it disappeared.
maybe it got stolen, maybe someone snatched it. maybe i dropped it.
dream logic refused to give me damn answers.
all i knew my diploma was gone.

naturally, i went looking for it.
that was when i noticed 'her'.
not directly, never directly, just at the edge of my eyes.

a woman with long black hair and a white dress.
like every fucking horror movie ghost ever.
i couldn't see her face. only her silhouette. only to know she was there.
oddly enough, i wasn't scared.
annoyed, maybe.
concerned, sure.
but mostly, 

i wanted to fucking find that diploma.

meanwhile my classmates had other priorities.

"don't look back," they kept saying.

over and over and over again.

"don't look back"

which is incredibly unhelpful advice when you're trying to locate a missing important document.
so i ignored them.

every time i searched for the diploma, the woman got closer.
and every time she got closer, an earthquake would occur.
not a small one either.
the entire dream world would shake violently as though the tectonic plates themselves were emotionally invested in my educational college journey.

at some point, i realized there was a pattern.
if i stopped looking for the diploma, everything became calm.

but i couldn't let it go.
i needed to find it.
i wanted to see my name on it.
i wanted it because it was mine.
so i searched one last time.

then i found it.

a female classmate was holding it.
relief washed over me.
finally, the nightmare was over.

or so i thought.

my classmate looked terrified.
not of me.
of what was standing behind me.

"don't look back," she said.
again.

the woman was right behind me now.
close enough that i could feel her presence.
close enough that the air around my ear felt strangely warm.
then she whispered something.
i don't know what she said.
i couldn't understand a single word.

maybe it was a curse, 
maybe it was divine guidance, 
maybe the secret of the universe, 
but whatever it was, the second she spoke, the biggest earthquake yet erupted around us.

the ground shook.
everything shook.

and then -- 

I woke up.

unfortunately, i woke up, and it wasn't finished.
because the moment i opened my eyes, i realized i couldn't move.
sleep fucking paralysis,

so there i was, fresh out of a ghost-induced graduation ceremony, diploma hunting, trying to convince my body to move.

eventually i broke free.

sigh.

title: 06-07-2026 - sunday
body: saturday feels like a relief, and not at the same time. don't get me wrong, i love the free time. i love not having work hours. but i don't know. i just feel like there's something missing. maybe it's just me, but i always want to be occupied, doing something, or else my mind explodes. recently, i've been drowning myself in work, and i like the feeling of being important. but at the same time, people say it's unhealthy. they say it'll burn you out. but for me, it's like filling that hole inside me. the feeling of importance. purpose. family gives you purpose. a lover gives you purpose. a cat gives you purpose. but it's so weird that i always feel like i want more than what i have. i'm not content at all. what's missing? what's missing? i ask myself that all the time.

title: 06-11-2026 - thursday
body: recently, i've been working a lot. for the past few weeks, i've been helping out my coworkers with their tasks too. i didn't really mind at first. i like helping people when i can. but now, i think it's finally catching up to me. i'm fucking burnt out. depressed? i honestly don't know. all i know is that lately, i don't feel like eating. i don't feel like playing games. i don't feel excited about things the way i usually do. that optimism i normally carry around feels strangely absent. even my relationships feel different. people i'm usually close to suddenly feel far away. it's not that they've done anything wrong. i just don't feel like talking. i don't feel like hanging out. i don't even feel like being perceived. i just want to be alone. completely alone. and maybe, if i'm being honest, i want to be somewhere else too. somewhere far away from this country, from work, from responsibilities, from expectations. somewhere quiet where nobody needs anything from me for a while. maybe i'm just tired. or maybe i've been tired for much longer than i've allowed myself to admit. for now, i think i'll just sit with that feeling and hope tomorrow feels a little lighter.

title: 06-12-2026 - friday
body: today, i woke up at 10 a.m. and took a bath early. for some reason, everything felt a little lighter. i didn't have any strange dreams last night, and i felt better than i did yesterday. maybe it's because it's friday. friday means just one more day, and then i get to slow down and laze around a little more than usual. i talked to my mom today, and she seemed kinder than usual. it was nice. i also talked to a friend. nothing particularly different happened, but sometimes normal conversations are comforting in their own way. overall, it was an ordinary day. but after how heavy yesterday felt, ordinary is good. i'm just thankful that today was a little lighter. sometimes that's enough.

title: 06-17-2026 - wednesday
body: i cried today. my salary was delayed, and all i could think about was leaving. escaping. getting away from everything and everyone. why do adults always know exactly what to say to make you feel guilty? why can't they understand that maybe we want something else? we have dreams. we have lives of our own. we don't owe anyone our future. sometimes i wonder why we're expected to spend our lives following someone else's script. they chose to bring us into this world. why do we have to live by their expectations? their rules? their idea of what a good life looks like? i've never understood family. not really. i've never understood blood ties, loyalty, or why being related automatically means you have to stay. all my life, i've wanted distance. i've wanted freedom. i've wanted a life that belonged to me. i want something that's mine. something only mine. something, just once, to be mine. mine to choose. mine to keep. mine without guilt. mine without someone telling me what to do with it. when people talk about family, they talk about love, support, and belonging. all i've ever felt is anger. blame. resentment. pain. and maybe that's unfair. maybe it isn't. i just know i'm tired. tired of feeling guilty for wanting something different. tired of carrying expectations that were never mine. tired of being told who i should be. and if that makes me lonely, then so be it. if choosing myself means walking alone for a while, then fine. at least i'll be walking toward something i chose.

title: 06-23-2026 - tuesday
body: today, i watched Anne with an E, and i was reminded of how beautiful a story can be. anne is such a blabbermouth, and somehow that is exactly what makes her lovable. she says whatever comes to mind, asks questions that others are too afraid to ask, and sees the world through wonder instead of fear. one line that stood out to me was: "if children are such a burden, why do people have so many of them?" it sounds simple, but it made me think. a child is like a sponge. a blank canvas. they absorb everything around them. the words they hear, the things they see, the values they are taught, and even the things adults do not realize they are teaching. whether good or bad, a child will always be influenced by their environment. watching anne made me think about how much responsibility comes with raising a child. children do not simply listen to what we say. they watch what we do. what i love most about anne is how vocal she is. she does not make herself smaller for the comfort of others. she speaks her mind, asks questions, and refuses to be ashamed of who she is. honestly, i wish i could be more like that. no one should ever make you feel lesser than yourself. and damn, imagination really is a beautiful thing. the way anne can turn ordinary things into something magical makes me realize how important curiosity is. somewhere along the way, many of us stop asking questions. we stop wondering. we stop imagining. but maybe life becomes a little brighter when we allow ourselves to be curious again. today reminded me that there is nothing wrong with taking up space, asking questions, and dreaming beyond what is in front of you. sometimes, the world feels a little kinder when you look at it through the eyes of someone who still believes there is magic in it. sometimes, growing up means keeping that sense of wonder alive, even when the world tries its best to take it away (aside from that, i still didnt receive my salary for this month.. ahh!!!)
